findings.reason: The protected SQL solution self-joins LogInfo on matching account_id, differing ip_address, and overlapping time intervals (first_session.login <= second_session.logout AND second_session.login <= first_session.logout), selecting DISTINCT account_id ordered by account_id ASC. The self-join solution is canonical, concise, and optimal; no candidate is required.

Matching account_id and differing ip_address isolates sessions for the same user from distinct locations. The interval condition login1 <= logout2 AND login2 <= logout1 tests closed time interval overlap completely, and DISTINCT account_id avoids duplicate output rows.

Self-joining R log rows by account_id and comparing timestamps takes worst-case O(R^2) time on all-one-account inputs, or expected O(R log R) / O(R) time with per-account indexing/hashing. Deduplicating B banned accounts uses O(B) space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs single column account_id, requires distinct IP addresses for temporal overlap violations, and returns each banned account exactly once.

The approach accurately details self-joining LogInfo for distinct IPs, complete interval overlap logic (login1 <= logout2 AND login2 <= logout1), and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover correlated EXISTS subqueries, sweep line algorithms, same-IP overlaps, different accounts, contained intervals, shared endpoints, multiple violations, and sequential IP usage.
